# landing/ — marketing page

A static page: React 18 UMD with in-browser Babel, and no build step. Preview it with the `landing` entry in `.claude/launch.json`, which runs `dev_server.py`.

- **A plain reload can run stale `.jsx`.** In-browser Babel fetches it through the HTTP cache. Before reloading, run `fetch(url, {cache: 'reload'})` on each changed file.
- **On narrow screens the replay is pinned under the nav, and the layer follows the scroll.** Each step is at least as tall as the screen left below the replay (`--pin-h`, measured in `app/app.jsx`), so wherever the page stops on a step its text is readable. This works only because phones scroll freely; don't add snapping back.
- **The replay's canvas must not change size except on a real resize.** Each resize reallocates the canvas and rescales the fighters. So on narrow screens, size things in `svh` rather than `dvh` (the URL bar changes `dvh`), and fade the log instead of collapsing it.
- **Every claim must match what the code does today.** Don't add accuracy, latency or throughput figures, and don't describe a live mode as shipped. The owner chose facts over marketing numbers.
- **`app/data.js` is real pipeline data.** `export_data.py` generates it; run `ai/.venv/bin/python landing/export_data.py` from the repo root. Never hand-edit it. It holds keypoints only and no video frames, because the fight footage isn't ours to publish.
- **Red and blue always mean corners, and orange is only the brand and CTA colour**, so a strike mark never reads as a corner.
- **Token values in `app/site.css` mirror `frontend/src/index.css`**, so the page and the app look like one product. That means a flat `--bg` (no grain, no glow orbs), no glow shadows, and the app's corner blue `#60a5fa`, which `CORNER` in `app/stage.jsx` repeats for the canvas. When an app token changes, change it here too.
- **The call to action is the waitlist** (`WaitlistForm` in `app/app.jsx`), because sign-in is invite-only. Sign-in stays as a quieter link for people already invited. Never offer uploading: it's admin-only.
- **The form posts to its own origin, `/api/auth/waitlist`.** In production Caddy forwards that one path from the landing host to the backend (`deploy/Caddyfile`); locally `dev_server.py` does the same, so start the backend to submit. Don't call the app's hostname from the page: that would need CORS on the backend.
- **Never send the email address to analytics.** The `waitlist` event carries only `from`.
- **With a mouse, trackpad or keyboard, each scroll moves exactly one section.** `app/pager.js` does this, reading its stops from each element's `scroll-snap-align` in `app/site.css`, so a new section needs one; without it, the pager jumps straight past the section. The mobile layout (up to 899px wide) and touch screens scroll freely, with no snapping and no pager. Mandatory snapping kept stopping mid-section on phones, so don't turn on `scroll-snap-type` for them. The pager checks width as well as touch because DevTools device mode doesn't always emulate touch.
- **Analytics is Umami Cloud's free plan and must stay cookieless.** The owner won't show a consent banner, so never add GA, Clarity, session replay or anything else that sets cookies. Each stored event property counts against the monthly event cap, so keep properties to one per event. The website ID is in `index.html`, and the script doesn't load on localhost.

content.text:
I added SEO to the landing page. It renders and works locally, and the Caddyfile and structured data pass validation. Nothing is committed or deployed yet.

**The main problem:** the whole page is drawn by JavaScript (React with in-browser Babel), so any crawler that doesn't run JS saw an empty page. That includes most AI and link-preview crawlers. Google does run JS, but heavy client-side pages can still fail to get indexed.

What's changed:
- **Page head** ([index.html](landing/index.html)):
  - A new title aimed at what people search for: "Fightlytics: MMA strike tracking and fight video analysis".
  - A tighter description, plus robots, canonical and full Open Graph / Twitter tags.
  - Schema.org structured data describing the organisation, the website and the app.
- **Content without JavaScript:** a `<noscript>` block repeats the page's real copy (headings, the four steps, method and early-access note). Normal visitors never see it, and I checked it stays hidden in the browser.
- **New files in `landing/`:**
  - `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`.
  - `favicon.svg`, moved out of the inline data URI so search engines can fetch it.
  - `apple-touch-icon.png`.
  - `og.png`, the 1200×630 share image: headline plus one real frame of red/blue pose output from `app/data.js`.
  - `make_images.html`, a dev-only page that redraws the two PNGs.
- **[Caddyfile](deploy/Caddyfile):**
  - Production only serves an allowlist of paths, so I added the new files to it; without that they would return 404.
  - The app host now sends `noindex`, so its sign-in page doesn't compete with the landing page in search results.
- **[landing/CLAUDE.md](landing/CLAUDE.md):** rules for keeping the `<noscript>` copy in step with `app.jsx`, changing all absolute URLs together, and updating the Caddy allowlist.

**Decision for you:** I took `https://fightlytics.duckdns.org/` as the canonical address because that's where the page is live now. If you move to your own domain, change every URL listed in CLAUDE.md together. A domain you own will also rank better than a duckdns subdomain.

After you deploy:
1. Add the site in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
2. Submit `sitemap.xml` in both.
3. Paste the link into a link-preview checker to see the share card.

One remaining drag on speed rankings is that in-browser Babel compiles the page on every visit. Precompiling the JSX would fix that, but it means adding a build step, which the page deliberately doesn't have, so I left it alone.
Do not commit anything as per instructions

How do I run a landing page server?

From the repo root, run:

```bash
python3 landing/dev_server.py
```

Then open http://localhost:4321. To use a different port, add it at the end (for example `python3 landing/dev_server.py 8080`).

- **No install or build:** it only needs Python 3. It serves `landing/` as static files, the way Caddy does in production.
- **The waitlist form needs the backend:** the server passes `POST /api/auth/waitlist` to the backend on port 8000. If the backend isn't running, submitting the form fails with a 502. Start it with:

```bash
cd backend && .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

- **A normal reload can show old `.jsx`:** the page compiles its JSX in the browser, and the browser may serve a cached copy. If an edit doesn't show up, do a hard reload (Cmd+Shift+R).

I can also start it in the app's preview browser for you; it's set up there as the `landing` entry in `.claude/launch.json`.
